model.label: Observation density
model.question: How much fungal life is actually being found here?

submetrics.label: Observations per km²
submetrics.why: Research-grade iNaturalist fungi records per unit area.

submetrics.label: Fungal share of all observations
submetrics.why: Fungi as a share of all research-grade records; corrects for how popular iNaturalist is locally.

submetrics.label: GBIF records per km²
submetrics.why: Adds museum and national recording-scheme data.

model.label: Species richness
model.question: How many different fungi can you expect to meet?

submetrics.label: Species observed
submetrics.why: Distinct research-grade fungal taxa recorded within the radius.

model.label: Seasonal reliability
model.question: For how much of the year is there something to find?

submetrics.label: Reliable months
submetrics.why: Months holding at least 4 % of yearly records and at least 10 records.

submetrics.label: Climate suitability index
submetrics.why: Mean monthly product of a temperature window and a moisture factor (ERA5 normals).

submetrics.label: Woodland share of surrounding area
submetrics.why: Share of the circle mapped as forest/wood in OpenStreetMap; 60 % or more gives full marks.

exclusions.label: Observations per 100k residents
exclusions.reason: not available for 40 of 40 locations (e.g. vancouver); dropped for all so scores stay comparable

sources.title: iNaturalist research-grade observations
sources.provider: iNaturalist (California Academy of Sciences & National Geographic Society)
sources.license: Observation records CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-NC per observer; aggregate counts used here
sources.used_for: Observation density, fungal share, species richness, seasonal reliability
sources.retrieval: API v1 (api.inaturalist.org/v1): /observations (per_page=0 for totals), /observations/species_counts, /observations/histogram (date_field=observed, interval=month_of_year); filters taxon_id=47170 (Fungi), quality_grade=research, lat/lng/radius.

sources.title: iNaturalist observation coordinates (recent sample)
sources.license: Per-observation licences (CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-NC); only coordinates are binned
sources.retrieval: API v1 /observations with per_page=200, order_by=created_at, order=desc; the `location` field ("lat,lon") of each record is binned into a grid. Coordinates of obscured (sensitive) records are already randomised by iNaturalist.

sources.title: GBIF fungal occurrence records
sources.license: CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-NC per dataset; aggregate counts used here
sources.used_for: Record depth sub-metric of observation density
sources.retrieval: API v1 /occurrence/search with kingdomKey=5 (Fungi), geoDistance=<lat>,<lon>,<radius>km, hasGeospatialIssue=false, limit=0; the `count` field is used.

sources.title: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5 reanalysis)
sources.provider: Open-Meteo.com; ERA5 by Copernicus Climate Change Service / ECMWF
sources.used_for: Climate suitability (monthly temperature and precipitation normals)
sources.retrieval: archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive with daily=temperature_2m_mean,precipitation_sum, timezone=UTC over the configured period (default 2014-2023); reduced to 12 monthly normals.

sources.title: WorldPop global gridded population (100 m, unconstrained)
sources.retrieval: api.worldpop.org/v1/services/stats with dataset=wpgppop, year=2020 and a GeoJSON circle polygon; `data.total_population` is used (asynchronous tasks are polled).

sources.title: OpenStreetMap woodland polygons (landuse=forest, natural=wood)
sources.provider: OpenStreetMap contributors, queried through the Overpass API
sources.used_for: Habitat proximity (share of the surrounding area mapped as woodland)
sources.retrieval: overpass-api.de/api/interpreter, one query per location: for each point of a 7x7 lattice clipped to the circle, is_in(lat,lon) filtered to landuse=forest or natural=wood areas, `out count`. Forest share = points inside woodland / points (lower bound: woodland without an Overpass area is not seen).

top.sentence: Berlin (Germany) ranks first for a mushroom lover with 78.5 out of 100, ahead of Helsinki (Finland) with 74.2. Its biggest advantage is seasonal reliability (+3.3 points). Helsinki does better on observation density (+2.1 points).

verdict.sentence: Berlin (Germany) ranks first for a mushroom lover with 78.5 out of 100, ahead of Helsinki (Finland) with 74.2. Its biggest advantage is seasonal reliability (+3.3 points). Helsinki does better on observation density (+2.1 points).
